referenceInfo.title: Scoring Guide
referenceInfo.p1: Architecture: sex-specific dual-slope norms × nonlinear body-mass scaling. Below the 100-point elite benchmark, scores rise on a standard linear track; past that benchmark a gentler overclock slope keeps elite grips distinguishable while converging to the 200-point single-axis ceiling.
referenceInfo.p2: Sex-specific physiological input ceilings apply. Values above the ceiling are scored and stored at the ceiling as a measurement guardrail so extreme readings cannot warp the radar scale.
referenceInfo.p3: Source authority: norm distribution and ceilings reference IronMind Captains of Crush (CoC) elite-qualifier data, cross-checked against World's Strongest Man (WSM) historical record literature.
referenceInfo.p4: Benchmark inspiration draws from Magnus Samuelsson (1998 WSM champion; legendary certified closer of CoC No.4), representing the public elite tier this axis is designed to cover.
referenceInfo.p5: Product measurement guardrail — not a competition certification.
referenceInfo.p6: Scientific calibration follows allometric scaling (square–cube physiology): body mass is nonlinearly corrected to offset absolute-size advantages on the dynamometer. Male and female tracks use independent norms and ceilings to avoid unfair inflation from a single shared anchor.
referenceInfo.p7: Overclock band: past the 100-point elite benchmark, lighter athletes retain relative-strength expression while heavier frames stay competitive after mass scaling, with legend-tier aura bands still reachable and final scores converging to the 200-point single-axis ceiling.
referenceInfo.p8: Changing Home body weight will dynamically recalculate your grip axis score from the latest weight.
